subject: science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging KS3 exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for KS3 simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Work done and changes in energy of moving objects
Power ratings and energy usage in kWh
Dissipation of energy to the surroundings

questions.q: In which unit is energy measured?
questions.explain: Energy is measured in joules (J). Newtons measure force, watts measure power (energy per second) and metres measure distance.

questions.q: A moving car has energy in which store?
questions.explain: Any moving object has energy in its kinetic store. The faster or heavier it is, the more energy it holds there.

questions.q: Which of these is a way of transferring energy, NOT an energy store?
questions.explain: 'By heating' is a transfer pathway that moves energy between stores. Kinetic, chemical and gravitational are all stores where energy is held.

questions.q: A wind-up torch is wound and then glows. Which describes the transfer best?
options: Elastic store → light, mechanically then by radiation
questions.explain: Winding fills the elastic store; releasing it turns a generator (mechanically) and the bulb transfers energy away by radiation as light.

questions.lo: Work done and changes in energy of moving objects
questions.q: When a force moves an object, we say that:
questions.explain: When a force makes an object move, work is done. Doing work transfers energy from one store to another.

questions.lo: Work done and changes in energy of moving objects
questions.q: A crane slowly lifts a heavy container straight up. Which store gains the most energy?
questions.explain: Rising higher does work against gravity, so energy goes mainly into the gravitational store. Moving slowly means the kinetic store barely changes.

questions.lo: Work done and changes in energy of moving objects
questions.q: A ball is dropped from a window. As it falls, energy is transferred from which store to which store?
questions.explain: As the ball falls it loses height (gravitational store) and speeds up (kinetic store), so energy moves from the gravitational store to the kinetic store.

questions.q: In which store do both food and fuels hold their energy?
questions.explain: Food and fuels both hold energy in a chemical store, which is released when they are 'burned' (in a body or a fire).

questions.q: Food A gives 25 kJ per gram and food B gives 10 kJ per gram. What does this tell you?
options: Food B stores more energy per gram
Both store the same energy per gram
Food A stores more energy per gram
questions.explain: A higher kJ-per-gram value means more energy is stored in each gram, so food A stores more energy per gram than food B.

questions.q: A snack bar releases 6 kJ of energy per gram. How much energy is stored in a 30 g bar?
questions.explain: Energy = energy per gram × mass = 6 × 30 = 180 kJ.

questions.lo: Power ratings and energy usage in kWh
questions.q: What does the power rating of an appliance tell you?
options: How much it cost to buy
questions.explain: Power (in watts) is the rate of energy transfer. A higher power rating means the appliance transfers energy faster.

questions.lo: Power ratings and energy usage in kWh
questions.q: A 2000 W kettle and a 1000 W kettle both boil the same water. Which is true?
options: The 1000 W kettle transfers energy faster
The 2000 W kettle transfers energy faster
They transfer energy at the same rate
questions.explain: A higher power rating means faster energy transfer, so the 2000 W kettle transfers energy at twice the rate and boils the water sooner.

questions.lo: Power ratings and energy usage in kWh
questions.q: A 3 kW heater is switched on for 4 hours. How much energy does it use?
questions.explain: Energy (kWh) = power (kW) × time (h) = 3 × 4 = 12 kWh.

questions.q: An appliance uses 5 kWh of energy and each kWh costs 30p. What is the total cost?
questions.explain: Cost = energy used × price per kWh = 5 × 30p = 150p (£1.50).

questions.q: Two lamps do the same job. Lamp A is rated 60 W and lamp B is rated 10 W. Which cuts the electricity bill and why?
options: Lamp A, because higher power is cheaper
Lamp B, because it transfers less energy per second
Lamp A, because it is brighter
questions.explain: For the same job, the lower-power lamp (B) transfers less energy each second, so it uses fewer kWh and costs less to run.

questions.q: The law of conservation of energy says that energy:
options: Can be created but not destroyed
Can be destroyed but not created
questions.explain: Energy cannot be created or destroyed — it can only be transferred and stored. The total amount always stays the same.

questions.q: On a swing (ignoring friction), where does the bob have the most energy in its kinetic store?
options: Halfway up on the way down
questions.explain: At the lowest point almost all the gravitational store has become kinetic store, so the bob moves fastest and its kinetic store is largest there.

questions.lo: Dissipation of energy to the surroundings
questions.q: When we say energy is 'dissipated', we mean it is:
options: Spread out to the surroundings, usually by heating
Locked away forever in a chemical store
questions.explain: Dissipated energy spreads out to the surroundings, usually by heating, where it is too spread out to be useful. It is not destroyed — energy is still conserved.

questions.lo: Dissipation of energy to the surroundings
questions.q: A toy car rolls across the floor and slowly stops. What has happened to its kinetic-store energy?
options: It was used up so none is left
It was dissipated to the surroundings by heating due to friction
questions.explain: Friction dissipates the energy — it spreads out to the surroundings by heating. The energy still exists; it is just too spread out to be useful.

questions.lo: Dissipation of energy to the surroundings
questions.q: Which change would help a house's thermal store cool down most slowly and cut the heating bill?
questions.explain: Insulation slows the rate energy is transferred out by heating, so the home stays warm longer and less fuel is needed — cutting the bill.
